title: Rufiyaa Sign: Copy & Paste ⃂, the Maldives' Currency Symbol, Final in Unicode 18.0
meta_description: The Maldivian rufiyaa sign (⃂, U+20C2) was accepted by the Unicode Technical Committee in October 2025 and published in Unicode 18.0 on September 16, 2026, but no system font renders it yet. Here's its design, status, and what to type until then.
hero_tagline: The Maldives' own currency symbol, built from the Thaana letter ރ, published in Unicode 18.0 on September 16, 2026, though no keyboard or system font renders it yet.
intro: The rufiyaa sign (⃂, U+20C2) is the currency symbol for the Maldivian rufiyaa. Its design, by Hassan Shujau, takes the Thaana letter ރ (raa) (the first letter of ރުފިޔާ, rufiyaa) and adds a horizontal stroke across it, the same visual convention that turns a plain letter into a currency mark in the euro, yen and Indian rupee signs. Unicode's own allocation pipeline records the character as provisionally assigned on 2025-07-22 and formally accepted on 2025-10-29, under UTC decisions 184-C18 and 185-C40, and Unicode 18.0 published it on September 16, 2026. That status matters more than it sounds: published is not the same as available. Until vendors ship fonts covering the character, ⃂ will render as an empty box on almost every device, so the practical answer today is still MVR, Rf, or the Thaana letter ރ itself. This page carries the real codepoint so you can test it, and tells you honestly what to use while you wait.
sources: Unicode 18.0's publication on September 16, 2026, with this character as U+20C2 RUFIYAA SIGN, is confirmed by the Unicode Consortium's Unicode 18.0 announcement, which notes that vendors can now implement support. The Saudi riyal sign's Windows 11 support is in Microsoft's KB5070311 release notes, and its arrival on the iPhone keyboard rests on users' own posts from March 24, 2026 on X and Instagram.

symbols.label: Saudi Riyal Sign (U+20C1, final since Unicode 17.0)

faq.a: It is the currency symbol for the Maldivian rufiyaa, encoded at U+20C2. The design, by Hassan Shujau, is the Thaana letter ރ (raa), the first letter of ރުފިޔާ, with a horizontal stroke added across it, the same convention used by the euro, yen and Indian rupee signs.

faq.q: Why does the rufiyaa sign show as an empty box?
faq.a: Because your device's fonts don't cover it yet. The character was accepted by the Unicode Technical Committee on 29 October 2025 and published in Unicode 18.0 on 16 September 2026, and operating systems and font vendors add coverage only after publication, usually months later. As of September 25, 2026, an empty box is the expected result on almost every device.

faq.q: When can I actually type the rufiyaa sign?
faq.a: Not on a fixed date. Unicode 18.0 published the character on 16 September 2026, but that is when the standard defines it, not when your phone can draw it. As of September 25, 2026, no vendor has announced a date. Keyboard and font support follows separately, usually over the months and years after publication: the Saudi riyal sign, final a full version earlier, reached Windows 11 in December 2025 and the iPhone keyboard in March 2026, and is still rolling out elsewhere.

faq.q: What should I use for Maldivian rufiyaa instead?
faq.a: MVR is the ISO 4217 currency code and is unambiguous everywhere. Rf is the common short form. The Thaana letter ރ renders correctly on any device with Thaana support and is the closest visible relative of the new sign. Avoid the rupee sign ₨ if precision matters: it is a different currency's symbol.

faq.q: Is the rufiyaa sign the same as the rupee sign?
faq.a: No. The rupee sign ₨ (U+20A8) and the Indian rupee sign ₹ (U+20B9) belong to other currencies. The rufiyaa sign is its own character at U+20C2, built from Thaana rather than Latin or Devanagari letterforms, even though the currency name shares a root with rupee.

faq.q: Which other currency symbols are new in Unicode 18.0?
faq.a: Three sit together in consecutive codepoints: the rufiyaa sign at U+20C2, the UAE dirham sign at U+20C3, and the Omani rial sign at U+20C4. The Saudi riyal sign at U+20C1 is the neighbouring character that was finalised a version earlier, in Unicode 17.0.
